title: Capacity Triage Wizard: mapping enterprise SLA targets to GPU class & reserved throughput
creator: Diego Alvarez
description: Background: Enterprise sales and solutions teams are repeatedly asked to estimate reserved throughput and SLA targets for customers with heterogeneous workloads. Current intake is manual, error-prone, and often mismatches GPU family preference vs. latency/throughput expectations. Goal: ship a 'Capacity Triage Wizard' in the intake flow that translates customer SLA fingerprints (p99 latency, throughput RPS, expected token lengths, burst tolerance) into recommended reserved throughput bundles and GPU-family affinity, with a confidence score and explicit fallback policy. Scope: - UI-first intake assistant for customer success & sales (Console + form) - Heuristic engine that matches SLA fingerprint to GPU class (A100/H100/RTX/TPU-like families) and reserved throughput bands - Output includes: recommended reservation (GPU count + family), suggested scaling policy (autoscale thresholds, burst buffer), expected cost tier estimate, and rollback/fallback options. Non-goals: automated provisioning, contractual negotiation automation, or replacing dedicated capacity sizing review. Rationale: reduces time-to-response for enterprise intake, decreases mis-provisioned reserved pools, and improves SLA adherence during onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard accepts structured intake (p50/p95/p99 latency targets, RPS or tokens/sec, 99th percentile SLA, expected session length, burst profile)
Engine outputs a recommended reserved throughput band with a rationale sentence and confidence score
Recommendation includes a preferred GPU family and an alternate fallback family with conditions
UI shows cost delta estimate (low/med/high) and suggested autoscale/burst settings
At least two pilot customers successfully used the wizard and the recommendation matched the review by PM/ENG leads in >= 80% of cases
updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with Sales Eng, Solutions, and Runtime Eng. Captured common intake fields and failure modes (mis-sized pools, wrong GPU family) - notes in Confluence.

2026-03-05: Drafted SLA fingerprint model: inputs include median/percentile latencies, expected concurrency, token length distribution, and burst tolerance. Proposed scoring matrix for GPU affinity (compute-bound vs memory-bound).

2026-03-07: Eng agreed on a conservative mapping for H100 -> low-latency p99 < 200ms workloads; A100 -> high-throughput token-heavy jobs; RTX-class for dev/staging. Need kernel cost multipliers from infra team.

2026-03-09: UX sketch complete. Added inline explanation copy and 'why we recommended this' modal. UX review by Marina Liu (Design) - she requested clearer fallback language and a 'confidence' indicator.

2026-03-11: Built prototype scoring engine (spike) with two heuristics: latency-first and throughput-first. Early results on synthetic workloads show distinct recommendations; opened ENG spike ticket ENG-28421 to formalize algorithm.
2026-03-12: Demo to Solutions team; they requested CSV export of recommended settings and a linkable 'recommendation snapshot' for contract discussions. Added as follow-up.
comments: Ethan Cole (Solutions): 'This will save ~2-3 days per onboarding by avoiding back-and-forth sizing calls.'
Marina Liu (Design): 'Confidence bar and fallback family need clarifying copy. Also prefer verb 'preferred' rather than 'required'.'
Priya Kapoor (Sales Eng): 'Please include common regulatory constraints (e.g., EU-only regions) in the matching logic — affects GPU availability.'
Diego Alvarez (PM): 'Ensure recommendation includes an explicit operational fallback (eg. route to hosted pool with degraded SLA) for contractual safety.'
Eng lead (via ENG-28421): 'We should validate against historical dedicated intakes from the last 18 months to tune thresholds.'
test_plan:
- Generate synthetic intake forms across 6 workload archetypes (LLM chat low-latency; batch embedding high-throughput; reranker mixed) and assert recommendations map to expected GPU families.
- Run recommendations against 12 anonymized historical enterprise intakes and compute match rate vs. post-onboarding final sizing.
- Manual review with Solutions and Runtime Eng on 3 pilot customers; collect qualitative feedback and adjust heuristics.
- Verify UI export and snapshot link functionality end-to-end in staging.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect GPU affinity leading to missed SLOs. Mitigation: conservative mapping and mandatory Eng review for high-confidence-impact customers.
Risk: Availability constraints in specific regions. Mitigation: surface region availability early in the intake and provide autoscale-to-hosted fallback.
Risk: Sales misuse (over-promising). Mitigation: include explicit 'estimation only' banner and require legal/contract team sign-off for SLA commitments.
